name: Pay For Post with WooCommerce
author: Matt Pramschufer

sections.description:
Quickly and easily sell access to pages, posts and custom post types through WooCommerce with Pay For Post with WooCommerce. I originally created this plugin because I looked everywhere, and I couldn’t find a plugin already out there, free or premium, that would do the simple fact of selling access to a particular page or post through WooCommerce. So I decided to write my own.

Requirements

  • WooCommerce version 2.6+ to be installed and active
  • Guest checkout to be turned OFF
  • PHP 7.4+ is required

How It Works

Getting everything setup will take you less than 5 minutes with three simple steps.

  • Step 1 Create a product in WooCommerce
  • Step 2 Create a page or post in WordPress
  • Step 3 Associate your product with your page using the Pay For Post with WooCommerce meta box.

It’s that simple.

With the Premium version, you have several other options for protecting content like, time based, number of page views, etc.

How-to Videos

How-to Install and Configure

How-to Protect a Page/Post

Demo

You can view a front-end demo by going to https://demo.pramadillo.com if you would like to schedule an admin demo please visit https://pramadillo.com/support and select Plugin Admin Demo.

Features

  • Restrict content from pages, posts and custom post types based on if they have purchased a specific WooCommerce product
  • Ability to protect a single post or multiple posts with a single product
  • Ability to protect posts with multiple products
  • Simple to use
  • Uses native WooCommerce functionality to ensure future compatibility
  • Global restricted content message which is used for all protected content
  • Utilize any standard WooCommerce shortcodes
  • PREMIUM ONLY Ability to override Restricted Content Message on a per page basis
  • PREMIUM ONLY Delay Restriction – This allows you to delay the paywall from appearing for a set amount of time.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Page View Restriction – This allows you to limit the number of page views the user who purchased this product has before the paywall reappears. Options to specify over a set amount of time or forever.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Expiry Restriction – This allows you to specify an expiration on this post which would require the user to repurchase the product associated with this post.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Custom WooCommerce tab on the My Account page to list out all purchased content
  • PREMIUM ONLY Listing of purchased content on order receipt and order confirmation page
  • PREMIUM ONLY PolyLang Multiple Language support
  • PREMIUM ONLY Priority Support
  • PREMIUM ONLY Woo Memberships Support!
  • PREMIUM ONLY Woo Subscriptions Support! (Simple and Variable subscription product types, and products sold on WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.0+ subscription plans)
  • PREMIUM ONLY Easily access all protected content and which users purchased them
  • PREMIUM ONLY Automatically add a lock icon to all protected posts
  • PREMIUM ONLY Show a list of content that gets unlocked by purchased product on product page.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Full Elementor Support. You can now protect every element differently on an Elementor page!

The premium version of this plugin consists of more advanced features to really get the most out of selling your pages and posts! To purchase the premium version please visit https://pramadillo.com/plugins/woocommerce-pay-per-post/

Shortcodes

[woocommerce-payperpost template='purchased']

This outputs an unordered list of the posts that have been purchased by the current user logged in.

There are several additional shortcodes available in the free and premium version. Take a look at https://pramadillo.com/plugins/woocommerce-pay-per-post/ for other available shortcodes.

Template Functions

IMPORTANT Out of the box this plugin will work with any theme which uses the standard WordPress function the_content(). For those themes that do not utilize the_content() you can use the following static functions in your templates.

Woocommerce_Pay_Per_Post_Helper::has_access()

This checks if the current user has access to the page. It returns true/false

Woocommerce_Pay_Per_Post_Helper::get_no_access_content()

This returns the content specified in the PPP Options.

For a full example of this take a look at https://pramadillo.com/plugins/woocommerce-pay-per-post/
sections.installation:
1. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  2. Browse to Admin->WooCommerce PayPerPost->Settings
  3. Go to Page or Post and you should see a meta box for Pay For Post with WooCommerce.
  4. You can find out more on how to install by visiting https://pramadillo.com/documentation/installing-woocommerce-pay-per-post/
sections.faq:
Do you offer installation and customization services?

Yes, if you need help with installation and/or would like additional customization work done for your website, you can fill out a request form at https://pramadillo.com/support

I wish this plugin had XZY feature

While I try to do my best to incorporate new features all the time, I implemented a new Feature Request board located at https://pramadillo.com/feature-requests

The output from the shortcode to display the products needed to purchase to view content looks weird

This is a default shortcode from WooCommerce. Take a look at https://docs.woocommerce.com/document/woocommerce-shortcodes/#section-9

Another thing you can try is to set the number of columns on the shortcode to disply only 1 column to do that you can change your shortcode to be [products ids='{{product_id}}’ cols=’1′]

Can this plugin work with custom post types?

Yes, this plugin worked with all custom post types. In the settings you can add and remove which post types you would like the metabox to show up on.

Does this work with WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.0 subscription plans?

Yes, in the premium version. WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.0 added subscription plans, which let any product be sold one-time, on a subscription, or both. Pay For Post decides by how the customer bought it. A customer who bought the product one-time has access permanently, like any ordinary purchase. A customer who bought it on a plan has access while that subscription is active or pending cancellation. When it is cancelled, expires or goes on hold, access ends, unless they also bought the product one-time.

The classic “Simple subscription” and “Variable subscription” product types work as before.

How do you link to your post after an order has been placed?

Use the premium version. 🙂 The premium version handles this for you. However, if you are using the free version what I have done in the past is use the Order Notes for the product in WooCommerce. So what will happen is after they purchase, on the Payment Received page they will see the order notes, and they will get sent in the receipt also.

So for instance, I have a Vimeo video that I embed in a page, on the Vimeo Product in WooCommerce I add the Password and notes on how to view the video, they gets transmitted via email and on the thank you page for the user.

For PREMIUM users, there is a built-in option to include the post links in the order email, confirmation screen and on the users My Account page.

Do I need to have user accounts turned on?

Yes, in order to keep track of who purchased what, it is a requirement that all customers have user accounts/

Do you offer support?

Yes, I do the absolute best I can to support the free version of the plugin. If you upgrade to the premium version you will have priority support.
sections.changelog:
=3.3.0=
* SECURITY – General security hardening.
* BUG FIX – Fixed a block editor save removing a post’s protection. A post protected in the classic editor, through the meta box with Block Editor Integration off, by an import, or before the block editor sidebar existed lost all its products, and so became free to read, the first time it was saved in the block editor, even if only the title changed. A post whose sidebar settings were left over from an earlier edit went back to those settings instead. Sidebar settings are now applied only when they were changed.
* BUG FIX – The block editor sidebar now shows a post’s products as selected when an import or other code stored their IDs as numbers. They appeared unselected, and the next change made in the sidebar removed them.
* BUG FIX – Fixed content lists, including the My Account Purchased Content tab, showing another list’s posts for up to an hour. Lists that differed only in their product_ids attribute or in a wc_pay_per_post_args filter shared one cached result. A wc_pay_per_post_args filter now takes effect immediately.
* BUG FIX – The Access Diagnostic’s purchase history now counts the same orders as the access check. It marked orders with no paid date as not counting, such as Cash on Delivery orders that have not been completed, and did the same to guest orders and orders on another account placed under the customer’s email address, so a report could say the customer has access while none of their orders counted. On Expiry and Page View pages it now names the order the access window is measured from, and says when that order has no paid date.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – A cancelled, expired or on-hold subscription bought through a WooCommerce Subscriptions plan kept access to protected content. After updating, those customers see the paywall. Stores using the classic subscription product types are unaffected.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Fixed a fatal error on the My Account Purchased Content tab when Polylang support is enabled.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Fixed a fatal error in the purchased-datatables list for any customer who had made a purchase. With Polylang support enabled it now keeps its table.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Purchased content lists no longer report posts with Expiry protection as expired while access is still valid. Only templates customised to show $post->expiration_status were affected.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – The inline shortcode’s paywall_message now offers the products that unlock the post the region is in, and its {{add_to_cart_link}} placeholder renders an add-to-cart link for each product. It rendered nothing before.
* NEW (PREMIUM) – Support for WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.0+ subscription plans. A product sold on plans unlocks content when the customer bought it one-time, or while they hold an active or pending-cancel subscription containing it. Classic subscription product types are unchanged.
* NEW (PREMIUM) – The Access Diagnostic explains a lapsed subscription plan instead of reporting that the customer never bought the product.
* NEW (PREMIUM) – wc_pay_per_post_is_subscription_plan_product filter. Return false to treat a product as an ordinary product, or true to keep the plan rule for a product whose plans were removed.
* NEW (PREMIUM) – Sort order for the Purchased Content tab on the WooCommerce My Account page. Under Settings > General Options, choose Title A–Z, Title Z–A, Newest published first, Oldest published first or Menu order for both lists on the tab. Newest published first remains the default, so nothing changes until you pick another order.
* NEW (PREMIUM) – wc_pay_per_post_my_account_shortcode_atts filter. Receives the shortcode attributes for each section of the Purchased Content tab and the section (has_access or purchased).
* NEW – wc_pay_per_post_shortcode_posts filter. Receives the list a [woocommerce-payperpost] template is about to render, already filtered and sorted, plus the template and the shortcode attributes.
* ENHANCEMENT (PREMIUM) – orderby=”title” on the [woocommerce-payperpost] shortcode now sorts titles naturally, so “Lesson 2” comes before “Lesson 10”.

=3.2.35=
* SECURITY – General security hardening.
* BUG FIX – Fixed a fatal error on the free version for any post configured with Delay, Page View or Expiry protection, typically settings left over from a premium licence that has since lapsed. Because the check runs through the_content, one such post took down every archive page listing it, for every visitor. Those posts now fall back to standard protection: still locked, purchase still required. The delay window, page-view allowance and expiry are simply not applied. Settings are untouched and resume if a licence is reactivated. An admin notice reports how many posts are affected.
* BUG FIX – The block editor bundle was served with no version number and no declared dependencies, so a browser or CDN holding an older copy had no reason to fetch an updated one, and editor packages could load in the wrong order. Both now come from the build manifest.
* BUG FIX – The block editor sidebar was built on an API WordPress deprecated in 6.6. It now uses the current API with a fallback for older WordPress, so the protection panel keeps working when the old one is removed.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – On sites using High-Performance Order Storage, Expiry and Page View protection could measure a customer’s access window from an older order than the one they had most recently placed. Sites on legacy order storage were unaffected.
* BUG FIX – Removed the false “you must enable custom field support” warning for custom post types that already had it enabled. The check ran before most post types were registered. Reported with Custom Post Type UI; it affected nearly every custom post type.
* NEW – Access Diagnostic on the Debug page. Enter a customer’s email address and the URL of the page they cannot open, and the plugin reports whether they have access and why: which products protect the page, which of them the customer bought, every order containing a required product and why each did or did not count, products they bought that do NOT unlock the page, and when access expires or how many page views remain. It runs the real protection engine as that customer, so its answer cannot differ from what the customer sees, and it never consumes a page view. A plain-text developer export with no personal data is included for support replies. It also flags configurations known to cause tickets: guest checkout enabled, protection disabled site-wide by the wcppp_is_active filter, and a WooCommerce Subscriptions compatibility layer supplying the subscription classes.
* NEW – Admin notice when posts are configured for Delay, Page View or Expiry protection on an install that cannot apply them.
* NEW – wc_pay_per_post_is_admin_call filter. Receives the is_admin() result and the post ID, and decides whether the protection engine takes its admin shortcut (which grants access to everything). Lets tools evaluate access from wp-admin and still get the front-end answer.
* NEW – Woocommerce_Pay_Per_Post_Helper::can_use_premium_protection(), the single gate for whether premium protection types may be applied.
* ENHANCEMENT (PREMIUM) – Subscription lookups are cached for the duration of a request. On a product page listing 60 unlocked posts this took database queries from 69 to 6. The cache is cleared when a subscription changes status.
* ENHANCEMENT – The block editor bundle is now built in production mode: 466 KB down to 97 KB, no functional change.
* UPDATE – Updated Freemius SDK to the latest version
* UPDATE – Tested up to WordPress 7.1
* UPDATE – Tested up to WooCommerce 11.2.1
* UPDATE (PREMIUM) – Tested with Elementor 4.3.4 and Elementor Pro 4.3.1
* KNOWN LIMITATION (PREMIUM) – WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.0+ can sell any product on a subscription plan, and its classic Simple/Variable subscription product types are off by default on new stores. Pay For Post recognises subscriptions by the classic product types only. A product sold through a subscription plan still unlocks the page, but its subscription status is not checked, so cancelling does not remove access. Stores using the classic product types are unaffected. Subscription plan support is planned for the next release.

=3.2.34=
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Fixed expire protection reloading a page over and over. The countdown that ends timed access on an open page was scheduled even when the expiry had already passed while the visitor could still see the content, so the page reloaded roughly once a second. Timed access that is genuinely still running is unaffected and still ends on the page the visitor is on.
* BUG FIX – Fixed the debug log reporting the opposite of the access decision it had just made, which made access issues much harder to diagnose. The access decision itself was always correct.
* ENHANCEMENT – The access check is now performed once per request instead of twice, removing duplicate database queries on every protected page.
* ENHANCEMENT – Added the wc_pay_per_post_can_use_woocommerce_subscriptions filter. Pay For Post detects WooCommerce Subscriptions by class name, which also matches plugins that ship a WooCommerce Subscriptions compatibility layer (such as Flexible Subscriptions by WP Desk). On those stores a subscription product requires both a purchase and an active subscription record, so customers who paid can be refused if no subscription record was created. Returning false treats those products as ordinary purchases so purchase plus expiration works as configured: add_filter( ‘wc_pay_per_post_can_use_woocommerce_subscriptions’, ‘__return_false’ );
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Page View Restriction now grants exactly the number of views configured. Previously the view being served was not counted until after access had been granted, so a post set to 3 views was readable 4 times and the paywall appeared on the 5th load. A post set to 3 views is now readable 3 times, with the paywall on the 4th. This also corrects the “Page Views: X out of Y” line, which previously showed 0 out of Y on the first view.
* UPDATE (PREMIUM) – The wc_pay_per_post_enable_pageview_fix filter now defaults to true. Sites that want the previous, more lenient count back can restore it with: add_filter( ‘wc_pay_per_post_enable_pageview_fix’, ‘__return_false’ );
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Fixed page view counter not resetting when a user repurchases access to a page/post. Views recorded before the new purchase no longer count against the new allowance.
* BUG FIX (PREMIUM) – Fixed Elementor element-level protection showing the paywall to users who had already purchased access. Elementor’s per-document element cache stored the paywalled markup and served it to everyone; the cache is now cleared and bypassed on PPP-protected documents.
* UPDATE – Updated Freemius SDK to v2.13.4
* UPDATE – Tested up to WordPress 7.0.2
* UPDATE – Tested up to WooCommerce 10.9.4
* UPDATE (PREMIUM) – Tested with Elementor and Elementor Pro 4.2.0

=3.2.33=
* BUG FIX – Fixed fatal error when using the purchased content shortcode on free version of the plugin.

short_description: Sell Pages/Posts through WooCommerce 2.6+ quickly and easily. Tested up to WooCommerce Version 11.2.x
description:
Quickly and easily sell access to pages, posts and custom post types through WooCommerce with Pay For Post with WooCommerce. I originally created this plugin because I looked everywhere, and I couldn’t find a plugin already out there, free or premium, that would do the simple fact of selling access to a particular page or post through WooCommerce. So I decided to write my own.

Requirements

  • WooCommerce version 2.6+ to be installed and active
  • Guest checkout to be turned OFF
  • PHP 7.4+ is required

How It Works

Getting everything setup will take you less than 5 minutes with three simple steps.

  • Step 1 Create a product in WooCommerce
  • Step 2 Create a page or post in WordPress
  • Step 3 Associate your product with your page using the Pay For Post with WooCommerce meta box.

It’s that simple.

With the Premium version, you have several other options for protecting content like, time based, number of page views, etc.

How-to Videos

How-to Install and Configure

How-to Protect a Page/Post

Demo

You can view a front-end demo by going to https://demo.pramadillo.com if you would like to schedule an admin demo please visit https://pramadillo.com/support and select Plugin Admin Demo.

Features

  • Restrict content from pages, posts and custom post types based on if they have purchased a specific WooCommerce product
  • Ability to protect a single post or multiple posts with a single product
  • Ability to protect posts with multiple products
  • Simple to use
  • Uses native WooCommerce functionality to ensure future compatibility
  • Global restricted content message which is used for all protected content
  • Utilize any standard WooCommerce shortcodes
  • PREMIUM ONLY Ability to override Restricted Content Message on a per page basis
  • PREMIUM ONLY Delay Restriction – This allows you to delay the paywall from appearing for a set amount of time.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Page View Restriction – This allows you to limit the number of page views the user who purchased this product has before the paywall reappears. Options to specify over a set amount of time or forever.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Expiry Restriction – This allows you to specify an expiration on this post which would require the user to repurchase the product associated with this post.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Custom WooCommerce tab on the My Account page to list out all purchased content
  • PREMIUM ONLY Listing of purchased content on order receipt and order confirmation page
  • PREMIUM ONLY PolyLang Multiple Language support
  • PREMIUM ONLY Priority Support
  • PREMIUM ONLY Woo Memberships Support!
  • PREMIUM ONLY Woo Subscriptions Support! (Simple and Variable subscription product types, and products sold on WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.0+ subscription plans)
  • PREMIUM ONLY Easily access all protected content and which users purchased them
  • PREMIUM ONLY Automatically add a lock icon to all protected posts
  • PREMIUM ONLY Show a list of content that gets unlocked by purchased product on product page.
  • PREMIUM ONLY Full Elementor Support. You can now protect every element differently on an Elementor page!

The premium version of this plugin consists of more advanced features to really get the most out of selling your pages and posts! To purchase the premium version please visit https://pramadillo.com/plugins/woocommerce-pay-per-post/

Shortcodes

[woocommerce-payperpost template='purchased']

This outputs an unordered list of the posts that have been purchased by the current user logged in.

There are several additional shortcodes available in the free and premium version. Take a look at https://pramadillo.com/plugins/woocommerce-pay-per-post/ for other available shortcodes.

Template Functions

IMPORTANT Out of the box this plugin will work with any theme which uses the standard WordPress function the_content(). For those themes that do not utilize the_content() you can use the following static functions in your templates.

Woocommerce_Pay_Per_Post_Helper::has_access()

This checks if the current user has access to the page. It returns true/false

Woocommerce_Pay_Per_Post_Helper::get_no_access_content()

This returns the content specified in the PPP Options.

For a full example of this take a look at https://pramadillo.com/plugins/woocommerce-pay-per-post/

Behaviour changes: without a premium licence, Delay, Page View and Expiry posts fall back to standard protection (expiry is not enforced); on HPOS sites, Expiry and Page View measure from the most recent qualifying order.
